Dev notes

How the annotations are read from Figma #

The page mirrors the Layout view one-to-one (same artboards, same sections, same blocks). For each component instance in a block, the bound variables are read from the instance itself: fills and strokes on the root give background and stroke, cornerRadius the radius, auto-layout frames give padding and gap, every visible text layer gives its colour and text style, and nested instances (icons, avatars, badges, and anything 160 px or smaller) give their size and colour. Each token is resolved for that instance (resolveForConsumer), so the raw value is what the instance actually renders in the file's current mode.

Reading the table. Element is the Figma layer the row describes (the component itself first, then its layers, texts and parts). Token is the Figma variable name; Value is its resolved raw value. A stroke listed as weight 0 is bound on the layer but not drawn. A colour listed at @ 0% is a bound colour with zero alpha, i.e. transparent. A dash means the property is set directly with no variable bound.

Figma page List; nodes: Accordion List 107060:97321.

SublabelMetadata

SublabelMetadata
Layout is state, not structure. Expanded vs Collapsed only rotates the chevron — the children it discloses are the host's rows, not part of this component. Pair it with Nested Accordion rows for the inset children.
Accessibility

Accessibility #

  • Expose expanded state. The chevron rotation is visual-only; the row needs aria-expanded semantics (or the platform equivalent) and its children grouped under it.
  • The whole row is the toggle. The 12dp chevron is far below any target minimum — never make it the only tappable region.
  • Do not nest a second action in a toggle row. The right accessory inside a disclosure row creates two behaviours on one surface; if the accessory acts, give it a separate, named target.

Examples

Usage Examples #

Design team
crit-feedback
show-and-tell
Accessibility

Accessibility #

  • Nesting must be structural, not visual. The inset communicates hierarchy to sighted users only; expose the parent–child relationship as a group with a level, or a screen reader hears a flat list.
  • Unread carries the same duty as the flat rows. Bold + dot is visual-only; announce it.
  • Deep nesting compounds the inset. At 72dp per level a phone runs out of line length by the second level; the published set stops at one, and so should the product.

Examples

Usage Examples #

Yesterday
Sprint retro
Roadmap sync
Centred headers are date breaks, not section controls. They separate time-ordered content (“Yesterday”, “Last week”). Anything that filters, expands or carries a “See all” belongs to the left-aligned header.
Accessibility

Accessibility #

  • Expose it as a heading. A section header that is announced as plain text gives a screen-reader user no way to jump between sections.
  • Primary vs Subtle is colour-only. Same size, same weight — the emphasis distinction does not survive greyscale and must not carry meaning on its own.
  • If it is not interactive, do not publish states for it. Hover and Selected imply a tap target; a header that does nothing when tapped should stay at Rest.

Dev notes

How the annotations are read from Figma #

The page mirrors the Layout view one-to-one (same artboards, same sections, same blocks). For each component instance in a block, the bound variables are read from the instance itself: fills and strokes on the root give background and stroke, cornerRadius the radius, auto-layout frames give padding and gap, every visible text layer gives its colour and text style, and nested instances (icons, avatars, badges, and anything 160 px or smaller) give their size and colour. Each token is resolved for that instance (resolveForConsumer), so the raw value is what the instance actually renders in the file's current mode.

Reading the table. Element is the Figma layer the row describes (the component itself first, then its layers, texts and parts). Token is the Figma variable name; Value is its resolved raw value. A stroke listed as weight 0 is bound on the layer but not drawn. A colour listed at @ 0% is a bound colour with zero alpha, i.e. transparent. A dash means the property is set directly with no variable bound.

Design crit
Standup notes
The custom-header slot swaps the title for controls. Its published default is two Horizontal filter pills — the pattern for a section whose header is its filter bar. Do not combine it with the text title; the slot replaces, never accompanies.
Accessibility

Accessibility #

  • Heading first, control second. Expose the title as a heading; if the accordion boolean is on, the toggle needs expanded/collapsed semantics on top of it.
  • “See all” is a separate target. It sits inside the header row but acts independently — name it and size its hit area; the 20dp text line is not enough.
  • Large is Display type. SF Pro Display below 20dp degrades; the 22dp Title 2 is at the safe edge — do not scale it down for tight layouts, switch to Default instead.

Examples

Usage Examples #

Priya
Marco
Dana
Kat Larsson
The carousel is for people, the grid is for actions. A horizontally scrolling strip suits an unbounded set (contacts, members). A bounded set of equally weighted actions is a Tile grid.
Accessibility

Accessibility #

  • Horizontal scrolling must be reachable. Every item needs to be in the accessibility order even when scrolled out of view; announce the strip as a list with a count.
  • Labels truncate at 84dp. “Kat Larsson” barely fits at 11dp; the full name belongs in the accessible name, not just the clipped caption.
  • Selection is colour-only — the #f0f0f0 tint is the entire selected affordance. Announce it.

Examples

Usage Examples #

Notifications
Appearance
Privacy
Settings screens, not feeds. The inset group is the iOS settings idiom — a bounded set of related rows. Unbounded, time-ordered content belongs in a flat Generic List with section headers.
Accessibility

Accessibility #

  • The group is a semantic container. Announce it as a group so row position (“2 of 3”) is scoped to the section, not the whole screen.
  • #f5f5f5 on white is decoration. The container fill does not meet any contrast threshold and must not be the only grouping cue — the heading above the group carries the meaning.
  • Everything row-level applies unchanged — see Generic List · Accessibility.

Dev notes

How the annotations are read from Figma #

The page mirrors the Layout view one-to-one (same artboards, same sections, same blocks). For each component instance in a block, the bound variables are read from the instance itself: fills and strokes on the root give background and stroke, cornerRadius the radius, auto-layout frames give padding and gap, every visible text layer gives its colour and text style, and nested instances (icons, avatars, badges, and anything 160 px or smaller) give their size and colour. Each token is resolved for that instance (resolveForConsumer), so the raw value is what the instance actually renders in the file's current mode.

Reading the table. Element is the Figma layer the row describes (the component itself first, then its layers, texts and parts). Token is the Figma variable name; Value is its resolved raw value. A stroke listed as weight 0 is bound on the layer but not drawn. A colour listed at @ 0% is a bound colour with zero alpha, i.e. transparent. A dash means the property is set directly with no variable bound.

Usage Examples #

Segmented · chaptered recording
Continuous · simple playback
Indicator off — read-only progress
Thumb on means scrubbable; thumb off means read-only. The Current indicator boolean is the affordance contract — never show a thumb on a bar the user cannot drag.
Accessibility

Accessibility #

  • A 4dp track needs a 44dp gesture zone. The visible bar is nowhere near a touch target; the host must extend the draggable region far beyond it.
  • Expose it as an adjustable element with value, minimum and maximum — a scrub bar that is announced as an image is unusable.
  • Black-on-grey passes; the thumb is the risk. A white 16dp thumb over the white portion of a card relies entirely on Shadow 04 for visibility — keep the shadow.
  • Segment boundaries are information. If chapters matter, announce them (“chapter 2 of 3”); the 2dp gaps are invisible to a screen reader.
